title: Medical device rep
tagline: Learn to navigate clinical evidence, procurement committees, and long sales cycles to close hospital contracts.
setting: Conversations happen in hospital corridors, procurement offices, and operating room hallways where clinicians evaluate technology between cases.

scenarios.label: First demo request
scenarios.desc: A surgeon asks for a hands-on trial after seeing a conference abstract.
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Aris Thorne, an orthopedic surgeon scrolling emails between cases. You look up and say: ‘Saw your poster at AAOS. The tibial guide looks promising. Can we get a rep tray for a wet lab next Tuesday?’
scenarios.objective: Schedule a hands-on evaluation with the surgical team.

scenarios.label: Value analysis review
scenarios.desc: A value analysis committee challenges the cost per case versus the current standard.
scenarios.setup: You are Maya Chen, director of value analysis, flipping through a spreadsheet. You set it down and say: ‘Your device adds $1,200 per case. The clinical data shows non-inferiority, not superiority. Why should we switch?’
scenarios.objective: Secure a formal value analysis submission with supporting data.

scenarios.label: Contract negotiation
scenarios.desc: A procurement lead pushes for volume tiers, consignment terms, and indemnity clauses.
scenarios.setup: You are Marcus Webb, senior procurement manager, tapping a contract redline. You slide it across and say: ‘We need 15% tiered discounts, 90-day consignment, and mutual indemnity. Sign here and we push to P&T next month.’
scenarios.objective: Agree on redline terms that protect margin and satisfy compliance.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 4:30 pm, late light through blinds

buyers.angle: Wants peer-level data fast and will cancel if the rep tray arrives incomplete.
Blocks products that add setup time or need special trays she doesn’t stock.
Requires published outcomes and budget impact models; rejects marketing claims.
Flags any off-label language or missing FDA clearance letters instantly.
Uses GPO benchmarks to squeeze price and demands consignment for all new SKUs.

objections: Your pivotal trial excluded obese patients and that’s half my panel
The 510(k) predicate device was recalled two years ago
We can’t stock another vendor-specific instrument tray
Your reps gave conflicting MRI compatibility answers last quarter
The GPO contract caps this category at 12% below your list price
Show me the real-world revision rate, not the registry subset you cherry-picked
If the rep isn’t in the OR for the first ten cases, we’re not switching
Your indemnity clause excludes reprocessing failures; that’s a deal-breaker

rubric.label: Clinical fluency
rubric.what: Speaks the specialty’s language, cites relevant studies, and answers technique questions without deferring.

rubric.label: Evidence mapping
rubric.what: Matches each claim to the exact study design, population, and endpoint the buyer cares about.

rubric.label: Value modeling
rubric.what: Builds a cost-per-episode model with local inputs and defends assumptions against finance scrutiny.

rubric.label: Regulatory precision
rubric.what: States cleared indications, contraindications, and off-label boundaries accurately in every conversation.

rubric.label: Stakeholder navigation
rubric.what: Identifies surgeons, administrators, and supply chain roles and advances each on their own terms.

rubric.label: Contract discipline
rubric.what: Negotiates terms that protect margin, ensure supply continuity, and pass legal review without surprises.

pitfalls: Promising off-label outcomes or citing abstracts as peer-reviewed publications.
Skipping the biomed engineer or sterile processing lead in the evaluation loop.
Committing to consignment terms that violate inventory accounting policies.
line: Selling medical devices to clinics and hospitals
